# test_count_vowels.py

import pytest

from your_module import count_vowels  # Replace "your_module" with the actual module name


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "text, expected",
    [
        ("hello", 2),
        ("world", 1),
        ("aeiou", 5),
        ("AEIOU", 5),
        ("The quick brown fox", 5),
        ("Python", 1),
        ("", 0),
        ("bcdfg", 0),
        ("12345", 0),
        ("!@#$%", 0),
        ("a e i o u", 5),
        ("AaEeIiOoUu", 10),
    ],
)
def test_count_vowels_happy_path_and_edges(text, expected):
    assert count_vowels(text) == expected


def test_count_vowels_mixed_case_with_punctuation():
    assert count_vowels("Hello, World!") == 3


def test_count_vowels_repeated_vowels():
    assert count_vowels("aaaaeeeiiiiooooou") == 18


def test_count_vowels_does_not_count_y():
    assert count_vowels("rhythm") == 0


def test_count_vowels_does_not_count_accented_vowels():
    assert count_vowels("áéíóú") == 0


def test_count_vowels_counts_only_standard_vowels_in_unicode_text():
    assert count_vowels("café") == 1  # counts "a", not "é"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "invalid_input, expected_exception",
    [
        (None, AttributeError),
        (123, AttributeError),
        (["a", "e", "i"], AttributeError),
        (b"aeiou", TypeError),
    ],
)
def test_count_vowels_invalid_input(invalid_input, expected_exception):
    with pytest.raises(expected_exception):
        count_vowels(invalid_input)
